name: Badlands Overlook Free Dispersed Camping - Buffalo Gap National Grassland

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Wall Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for primitive dispersed camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted on Buffalo Gap National Grassland public lands along the rim overlooking Badlands National Park. Must park within designated pullout areas.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in prairie badlands soil, 200 feet from dry washes. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood; shortgrass prairie wood gathering non-existent.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in containerized fire pans or existing rock rings only due to extreme prairie grass fire hazard. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Strict Red Flag Warning fire bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state highway changing to unpaved dirt prairie rim road (SD-240 / Nomad View Road / FS 7158)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Flat dirt prairie rim road. Can turn slick gumbo mud when wet.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible along main dirt rim road in dry conditions; high clearance recommended for rough side spurs)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 4-5 bars 5G/LTE (30-80 Mbps download speed on open rim)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (Unobstructed high prairie rim overlooking Badlands National Park)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, high winds, spring rainstorms, muddy clay tracks.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot (85-98°F), intense solar radiation, late afternoon severe lightning / hail storms.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal prairie rim boondocking (60-75°F daytime, 35-45°F nights), crisp clear skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Severe cold High Plains winter (15-35°F daytime, sub-zero nights), strong winds.

dangers_and_hazards: High wind gusts (40+ mph) on open cliff edge
Prairie wildfires during dry Red Flag Warnings
Steep vertical cliff drop-offs into Badlands canyons
Prairie Rattlesnakes active in warm months

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional camper vehicle driving slowly on rim road
Wind howling over badland canyon rim

common_animals: Bison / American Buffalo (grazing in nearby Badlands NP)

human_demographics_and_culture: Full-time digital nomads (one of the most famous boondocking spots in North America), vanlifers, astrophotographers, and road trippers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Oglala Lakota Sioux indigenous traditions revere the Badlands ('Mako Sica') and surrounding high prairie rims as sacred ancestral spirit lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Profound spatial freedom, dramatic canyon cliff vistas, world-class 5G connected solar boondocking.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding path through badlands rock formations and shortgrass prairie

public_reviews_summary: World-famous boondocking location known as 'The Wall' or 'Nomad View'. Breathtaking canyon rim views combined with blazing fast 5G cell internet.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 night sky. Outstanding solar panel power generation.
